data.text:
A Valentine’s Day promotion meant to give discounts to couples is under fire for allegedly excluding non-straight diners. The Korean-style chain BBQ Chicken offered a 20% discount for couples spending at least ₱1,599 under its “Sarang Gobaek Day” promo, but reports indicate the deal was explicitly limited to straight pairs.

Reports say some customers were turned away from the promotion despite meeting the requirements, and while some were able to use other discounts, the exclusion left many feeling unwelcome on a holiday meant for love and connection. 

Critics pointed out that a promotion designed to reward customers instead created a public spectacle of exclusion, sparking online backlash and debate over whether marketing choices should dictate who is allowed to celebrate. Many called the move divisive and asked why paying customers should be denied a discount based on who they love.

Brands that openly exclude customers risk losing credibility, trust, and future business. Filipino diners notice when a company’s actions contradict its marketing, and in today’s connected world, those stories spread fast. Exclusion is no longer invisible, and it comes at a cost.

As of now, BBQ Chicken Philippines has yet to issue an official statement. Would you still dine here knowing some customers are explicitly left out?
